[LANG-1836] Make TypeUtils.containsTypeVariables and unrollVariables honour the owner type of a ParameterizedType (#1812)
* [LANG-1836] Make TypeUtils.containsTypeVariables and unrollVariables honour the owner type of a ParameterizedType

containsTypeVariables(Type) only inspected getActualTypeArguments() of a
ParameterizedType, so Outer<T>.Inner was reported as free of type
variables although its Javadoc promises a recursive check of the type's
parameterization. Now the owner type is checked as well, unless it is a
raw Class (for example Map.class owning Map.Entry<String, Integer>),
because the Class branch reports true for any class that merely declares
type parameters.

unrollVariables(Map, Type) had three related problems in its
ParameterizedType branch:

- The owner type was never unrolled, so Outer<T>.Inner<Integer> kept the
  unresolved owner even when T was mapped. The owner is now unrolled like
  the type arguments (again leaving a raw Class owner untouched) and the
  result i

fix(types): замечания ревью — ошибки Sonar и лишний индекс
Sonar завалил Quality Gate по рейтингу надёжности. Три ошибки, все настоящие:

`Environment` — запись с полем-массивом, у которой переопределены `equals` и `hashCode`, но
не `toString`: в отладке было видно ссылку вместо содержимого.

Две защитные проверки на отсутствие последнего токена (недоразобранный блок) Sonar считал
мёртвыми, потому что выводит `getStop()` как непустой. Убирать проверки нельзя — у неполного
разбора токена правда может не быть. Заменены на `requireNonNullElse`: поведение то же,
мёртвого условия нет.

Замечание Copilot по делу: в конструкторе `Новый Структура("К1, К2", З1, З2)` поля
добавлялись по одному, а набор типов неизменяем — на каждый ключ копировалась накопленная
карта. Собираются и добавляются разом, как уже сделано для операторов-мутаторов.

fix(aop): publish events through every registered Spring context
EventPublisherAspect is an AspectJ singleton with a single
applicationEventPublisher field. When multiple Spring contexts
coexist (e.g., a @DirtiesContext-marked test class is interleaved
with regular @SpringBootTest ones in the same JVM fork), the
LRU-driven unregister fallback can route events to the wrong
context's listeners. The right context's workspace-scoped beans
(LocationRepository, SymbolOccurrenceRepository) then never get
filled, producing flaky failures like TypeServiceTest 'Expected
size: 1 but was: 0 in: []'.

Switch to fan-out: keep a volatile snapshot of all registered
contexts and publish each event to every one of them. Each context
has its own listeners and its own workspace-scoped beans, so only
the originating context observes side effects; other contexts
process the event without touching unrelated state.

fix: handle stale workspace snapshot in Micrometer context propagation
WorkspaceThreadLocalAccessor.setValue(URI) threw IllegalStateException
when a @Scheduled task fired after its captured workspace had been
unregistered (e.g. after test or workspace removal). Micrometer captures
the context snapshot at task-decoration time, so by the time scheduling-1
executes, the URI is no longer in WorkspaceContextHolder's registry.

Fix (Variant 3): instead of throwing, log WARN and clear the ThreadLocal.
The scheduled task (ConfigurationFileSystemWatcher.watch) does not rely on
the Micrometer-propagated context — it sets its own via
WorkspaceContextHolder.run() on each tick — so a null context is safe.

  (normal cleanup path after setValue warning)

shared across all Spring contexts. The previous implementation of

  LinkedHashSet to preserve insertion order for deterministic fallback

  registers/unregisters its own context; each Spring context gets its own
  instance so @PreDestroy is scoped correctly

fix:[BACKLOG-50640] Giving pentaho_user schema ownership to preserve the behavior from hsqldb 2.3.2 allowing pentaho_user to see all schemas. (#6338)
HSQLDB does not support GRANT ... ON SCHEMA ... syntax, and each schema
has exactly one AUTHORIZATION (owner) which cannot be reassigned after
creation. Since PUBLIC and INFORMATION_SCHEMA are already owned by DBA/
SYSTEM, the only way to grant pentaho_user equivalent full access to
those schemas is via DBA role membership, which HSQLDB treats as a
proxy for full access to every schema. Granting DBA to pentaho_user is
for test/sample data purposes only.

Use return value of HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate() in all DAO save methods (#5769)
* Initial plan

* fix: capture return value of HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate() across all DAO files

After the Hibernate 7 migration, session.saveOrUpdate() was replaced with
HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate() which internally uses session.merge(). Unlike
saveOrUpdate(), merge() returns a NEW managed entity instance. Discarding
the return value causes callers to get back the original (potentially
detached) entity, which can cause issues.

This commit fixes all DAO methods that were ignoring the return value of
HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate() and instead returning the original entity.
For methods returning the entity directly, the fix is to return the result
of saveOrUpdate(). For methods that use the entity after the call, the
result is assigned back to the variable.

Docs: Add Hive Metastore schema validation warnings for schema evolution with Hive catalog (#15814)
* Docs: Add Hive Metastore schema validation warnings for DROP COLUMN and REORDER

When using a Hive catalog, ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN (non-last column) and
ALTER COLUMN REORDER fail because the Hive Metastore validates schema
changes by comparing column types positionally. Dropping a middle column
shifts subsequent columns, causing HMS to reject the change as an
incompatible type change via MetaStoreUtils#throwExceptionIfIncompatibleColTypeChange.

Add warning admonitions to spark-ddl.md (DROP COLUMN and REORDER sections)
and flink-ddl.md (Hive catalog section) documenting the limitation,
workaround (hive.metastore.disallow.incompatible.col.type.changes=false),
and trade-off (Hive engine can no longer read the table).

fix: invoke RedisRateLimiter error callback/logging inside onErrorResume (#6645) (#7029)
* fix: invoke RedisRateLimiter error callback/logging inside onErrorResume (#6645)

onErrorResume absorbed every Redis error into a normal Flux.just(1L, -1L)
emission, so the trailing doOnError (which logged the error and invoked
the rate limiter algorithm's callback, e.g. cleanup of optimistically
written keys) was unreachable dead code. On a Redis outage every request
was silently fail-opened with no log signal and no cleanup callback.

Move the callback invocation and error logging into the onErrorResume
lambda itself so they actually execute when Redis errors occur.

* Improve error handling in RedisRateLimiter

* fix(deps): update dependency org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5 to v5.6.1

* Guard GZipDecoder against already-decoded streams

HttpClient 5.6.x changed content compression handling in ContentCompressionExec to a decoder pipeline and no longer reliably strips compression headers from the original response message. In that setup, Dropwizard can see Content-Encoding: gzip while the payload has already been decompressed.

GZipDecoder previously wrapped based on header alone, which can cause double-decoding failures. This change makes decoding defensive by skipping re-wrap for existing GZIPInputStreams and sniffing the gzip magic bytes before creating a new GZIPInputStream.

[PDI-20902] Share one server session across web service ports
Pan reported "Invalid cookie" warnings and HTTP 401 stack traces while
disconnecting from the repository, a regression introduced by the
PDI-20652 logout change.

Each JAX-WS port was getting its own cookie jar: the JAX-WS RI merges a
fresh HttpConfigFeature into every port's binding, and each of those
builds its own java.net.CookieManager. A single repository connection
therefore opened a separate HttpSession per service. close() then called
logout() on every cached port, and because the server-side logout
listeners are keyed by user rather than by session, the first logout tore
down state the remaining sessions still needed and they came back 401.

Give the manager one CookieManager, shared by every port via
HttpConfigFeature, so a connection uses a single server session. close()
now logs out exactly once, treats a 401 as an already-closed session, and
clears the shared cookie jar so a later connection cannot replay a stal

fix:[BACKLOG-50640] Giving pentaho_user schema ownership to preserve the behavior from hsqldb 2.3.2 allowing pentaho_user to see all schemas. (#10692)
HSQLDB does not support GRANT ... ON SCHEMA ... syntax, and each schema
has exactly one AUTHORIZATION (owner) which cannot be reassigned after
creation. Since PUBLIC and INFORMATION_SCHEMA are already owned by DBA/
SYSTEM, the only way to grant pentaho_user equivalent full access to
those schemas is via DBA role membership, which HSQLDB treats as a
proxy for full access to every schema. Granting DBA to pentaho_user is
for test/sample data purposes only.

(which backs DatabaseMetaData#getSchemas()), so it now only returns
schemas the connecting user directly owns or has DBA-role membership
over. Users granted only table-level SELECT privileges (e.g. the

in the Database Explorer, even though the tables inside are fully
queryable. This was a regression introduced when hsqldb was upgraded
from 2.3.2 to 2.7.4; sampledata.script content was verified not to be
the cause.

following the same extension point used by MSSQLServerDatabaseMeta,

Add predictive back for main activity exit (#8356)
### Description

`OpenDefaultPageBackPressedCallback` was always enabled (`super(true)`),
meaning it intercepted every back gesture including the final app-exit
one, preventing the system from running its predictive back animation on
Android 13+.

The fix: disable the callback when no custom back action applies, so the
system owns the final exit gesture entirely.

- **`updateMainBackCallbackEnabledState()`** — new method that enables
the callback iff any of these hold:
  - fragment back stack has entries (pop)
- current page ≠ default page and default page isn't
`DEFAULT_PAGE_REMEMBER` (navigate home)
- `backButtonOpensDrawer` is set, drawer is present, bottom nav is
absent, **and drawer is currently closed** (open drawer)
- **Constructor** changed from `super(true)` → `super(false)`; state is
computed on first navigation call
- **`FragmentManager.OnBackStackChangedListener`** registered in
`onCreate()` to update on back stack changes

Fail the AWS Kinesis input on unrecoverable AWS authorization denials (#26898)
* Fail the AWS Kinesis input on unrecoverable AWS authorization denials

The Kinesis Client Library retries its own DynamoDB calls on a fixed
schedule for as long as the input runs and only logs the failure, so a
missing IAM permission produces an endless ERROR loop while the input
consumes no records and still reports RUNNING. KCL offers no hook to
observe or stop that, but we build the AWS clients it uses, so an
ExecutionInterceptor on those clients can see every denial.

After three consecutive denials the input is set to FAILING with the
denied action and resource, and the KCL scheduler is stopped.

entity" when a view referenced a stream that could not be resolved to a
native stream. The view-side resolvers threw a ContentPackException,
which aborted and rolled back the entire content pack installation.

This was asymmetric with the export side (WidgetDTO.toContentPackEntity),
which already silently drops stream references it cannot map. Make the
three import-time view resolvers behave the same way: skip an
unresolvable stream reference with a warning instead of throwing, so a
single dangling reference no longer blocks the whole install.

The wrong-type branch (a non-null, non-Stream value) still throws, since
that indicates a genuinely corrupt entity map rather than a missing
reference.

Affected resolvers:
- WidgetEntity.toNativeEntity
- SearchTypeEntity.mappedStre

* ES|QL: HIGHLIGHT across FORK and UNION ALL

FORK and UNION ALL output merged columns as reference attributes, which
carry no mapping, so HIGHLIGHT analyzed them with standard. The new
ResolveHighlightFieldMappings rule gives HIGHLIGHT the mapping all
branches agree on, one that names each index's analyzer when branches

Adds a dynamic node-scope setting to control TorchScript model graph
validation. When set to false, the pytorch_inference process is
launched with --skipModelValidation, bypassing the operation
allowlist/forbidden list check.

types (self-managed, Cloud, serverless) via the cluster settings API,
without requiring infrastructure access or a rebuild.

The setting is dynamic - changes take effect on the next model
deployment without restarting the node.

CLI flag to the pytorch_inference binary.

Adding base64 indexing for vector values (#137072)
This adds support for indexing vectors via base64. Parsing floating
point arrays in JSON is...not cheap. So, if we encode the bytes in a
string, then we improve throughput.

Example python transforming a file (thank you copilot...)

```python
def base64_vector(dims):
    vec = np.random.rand(dims).astype(np.float32)
    # switch from default local of little endian to big endian
    byte_array = vec.byteswap().tobytes()
    # encode as base64
    return base64.b64encode(byte_array).decode("utf-8")
```

ESQL: LOOKUP JOIN with expressions (#134098)
Add support for LOOKUP JOIN with expressions.

FROM index1
| LOOKUP JOIN lookup_index on left_field1 > right_field1 AND left_field2 <= right_field2 AND left_field3 == right_field1
--handle name conflict with rename
FROM index1
| RENAME id as id_left
| LOOKUP JOIN lookup_index on id_left >=id AND left_field2 <= right_field2
Add support for 1 or more join predicate expressions in the ON clause of the LOOKUP JOIN. If there is more than one predicate expression, the predicate expression must be connected with the AND operator. Each predicate is in the form field1 BINARY_OPERATOR field2. One of them should be from the left and the other from the right. BINARY_OPERATOR is one of ==, >,<, >=, <=, !=. The same field can be used multiple times in the join on condition. If the fields in the join on conditions have the same name, they should be renamed so that the fields in the join on condition have unique names.

#42156 fix(ai): resolve relative paths correctly against a base URL with no trailing slash (#42157)
* #42156 fix(ai): resolve relative paths correctly against a base URL with no trailing slash

AIHttpUtils.resolve(base, paths...) built the request URI with plain
URI.resolve(path). Per RFC 3986, relative-reference resolution treats
the segment after the last "/" in the base as a file name, not a
directory, so resolving a relative path against a base without a
trailing slash replaces that last segment instead of appending to it:

  new URI("http://localhost:11434/v1").resolve("models")
  -> http://localhost:11434/models   (drops "/v1")

Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio) are
commonly configured without the trailing slash, which turns model
listing and chat completion requests alike into 404s - the likely
cause of several "connection test passes but chat 404s" reports on
the local-LLM feature request thread (#36951).

Normalize the base to end with "/" befor

Close channel on TLS exception to prevent half-open connections (#16202)
* fix: close channel on TLS exception to prevent half-open connections

SslServerTlsHandler.exceptionCaught() only logged the error without
closing the channel or propagating the exception. This caused channels
to remain TCP-active but application-dead when exceptions like
NoClassDefFoundError occurred during Netty read loops.

Similarly, SslClientTlsHandler did not close the channel on TLS
handshake failure, only firing exceptionCaught to downstream handlers.

This fix ensures both handlers close the channel on failure, allowing
Dubbo's existing health-check mechanism (isAvailable/addInvalidateInvoker)
to properly detect and remove broken invokers.

Refuse to emit account-purged without a pre-removal snapshot
The snapshot is the only evidence a deletion was a real purge, and the
localRemovalOnly check silently did nothing when it was missing -- so a federated
READ_ONLY / UNSYNCED account could be reported as purged while it still exists.

Nothing downstream catches that. With no snapshot the user is unresolvable, the
listener's subject gate skips a null user entirely rather than failing closed, and
the dispatcher delivers an unresolvable subject under default_subjects=ALL on the
benefit of the doubt. The admin path bails on a null user; the self-service
DELETE_ACCOUNT path does not, which is where it leaks.

Nor is the miss unlikely for the population at risk. Capture is best-effort and

opt-ins as supported extension points, with a worked isInNotifyGroup example.
The snapshot never populated either, so AbstractInMemoryUserAdapter reported an

consistent with the server-side password policy.

Fix SAML v2 API: null/omitted string attributes now remove model attributes (#51252)
* Initial plan

* Fix SAML null attribute removal in SAMLClientModelMapper

When a SAML client attribute is set to null (via PATCH with explicit null
or PUT omitting the field), the v2 mapper now removes the corresponding
model attribute instead of silently ignoring the null value.

Previously, `setAttributeIfNotNull` and `setBooleanAttributeIfNotNull`
would skip null values, leaving stale attributes (e.g. signingCertificate)
in place. This was a security concern since an administrator who PATCHed
`signingCertificate: null` would receive a 200 but the old certificate
would still be trusted for SAML signature verification.

Closes #51213

Deprecate the Twitter Identity Broker
Fix #44013

The Twitter broker relies on the unmaintained twitter4j library (no release in several years) and Twitter's legacy OAuth 1.0a endpoints. twitter4j uses Java serialization to record its state, which recurs as noise in security reviews.

This deprecates the broker behind a disabled-by-default feature (twitter-broker), mirroring the Instagram broker deprecation. As Twitter(X) now supports OAuth 2.0, the generic OAuth v2 identity provider can be used as a replacement, and the admin guide documents the migration.

Paginate UserSelect autocomplete and surface exact username match (#50185)
* Paginate UserSelect autocomplete and surface exact username match

The shared UserSelect typeahead fetched at most 20 users with no
pagination. When more than 20 users matched the typed term the target
user could not be selected (e.g. typing the full username "jack" only
listed 001jack..020jack, which sort first). This was a regression from
the legacy Admin UI, which paginated.

Fetch max+1 to detect further results and render a "Show more" entry
that loads the next page (reusing the existing showMore message), and
run a parallel exact-username lookup so a fully typed username is shown
at the top of the list. Pagination resets to the first page together
with the debounced search term, and the menu is height-capped and
scrollable so a long list does not stretch the page. The "Show more"
entry shows a loading spinner while the next page is fetched.

Closes #49702

KAFKA-20735: Skip state-directory lock on close when there are no sto… (#22951)
With the state updater enabled, Streams could log a spurious WARN
(previously ERROR) — "Unable to acquire lock while closing the state
store for task " — during back-to-back rebalances, when a task's
per-task state-directory lock is transiently held by another thread as
the task is handed off. It's harmless (no data loss or lag) but pollutes
alerting.

StateManagerUtil.closeStateManager() now short-circuits when there is
nothing to close: if the state manager has no registered stores and
we're not wiping state, it returns early without acquiring the lock or
logging. When stores are still registered but the lock can't be
acquired, the WARN is still emitted, preserving signal for genuinely
unexpected failures. The unclean-EOS wipe path is unchanged.

Add package-private ProcessorStateManager.hasRegisteredStores().  Guard
the lock/close/log in closeStateManager() with !wipeStateStore &&
!stateMgr.hasRegistered

handling for Streams groups:

KAFKA-19521: Fix consumption and leaving group when source topic is deleted (#20735)
Integration tests expecting `MissingSourceTopicException` were timing
out and taking 5+ minutes because [PR
#20284](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/20284) set the missing
topics timeout to `max.poll.interval.ms` (default 300 seconds).

This is inappropriate because:
- When source topics don't exist, actual poll frequency is `poll.ms`
(100ms), not `max.poll.interval.ms`
- The exception should be raised much faster based on heartbeat
frequency

Use `2 * heartbeatIntervalMs` (from broker via KIP-1071) as the timeout
instead:
- Ensures at least one heartbeat is sent before raising the exception
- Falls back to `max.poll.interval.ms` for backward compatibility
- Fixes slow integration tests

## Changes

1. Track `heartbeatIntervalMs` in `StreamsRebalanceData` and update it
on each heartbeat response
2. Use `2 * heartbeatIntervalMs` as timeout in

KAFKA-19730: StreamsGroupDescribe result is missing topology (#20574)
When toology not configured.

In the streams group heartbeat, we validate the topology set for the
group against the topic metadata, to generate the "configured topology"
which has a specific number of partitions for each topic.

In streams group describe, we use the configured topology to expose this
information to the user. However, we leave the topology information as
null in the streams group describe response, if the topology is not
configured. This triggers an IllegalStateException in the admin client
implementation.

Instead, we should expose the unconfigured topology when the configured
topology is not available, which will still expose useful information.

KAFKA-19694: Trigger StreamsRebalanceListener in Consumer.close (#20511)
In the consumer, we invoke the consumer rebalance onPartitionRevoked or
onPartitionLost callbacks, when the consumer closes. The point is that
the application may want to commit, or wipe the state if we are closing
unsuccessfully.

In the StreamsRebalanceListener, we did not implement this behavior,
which means when closing the consumer we may lose some progress, and in
the worst case also miss that we have to wipe our local state state
since we got fenced.

In this PR we implement StreamsRebalanceListenerInvoker, very similarly
to ConsumerRebalanceListenerInvoker and invoke it in Consumer.close.

MINOR: Deflake and improve SmokeTestDriverIntegrationTest (#20509)
This improves the SmokeTestDriverIntegrationTest in three ways:

1) If a SmokeTestClient fails (enters a terminal ERROR state), the
SmokeTestDriverIntegrationTest currently times out, because it keeps
waiting for state NOT_RUNNING. This makes debugging quite difficult.
This minor  change makes sure to just fail the test immediately, if a
SmokeTestClient enters the ERROR state.

2) If a test times out or fails prematurely, because a SmokeTestClient
crashed, the SmokeTestClients aren't shut down correctly, which will
affect the following test runs. Therefore, I am adding clean-up logic
that running SmokeTestClients in `@AfterAll`.

3) Finally, I found that the processingThread variation of this thread
triggers a subtle race condition. Since this features is currently not
actively developed, I disabled those variations and created a ticket to
reactivate the test.

Regenerates the SDK for `feat(ui): inform users about potential breaking changes after an upgrade` and `fix(system): align H2, Postgres and MySQL indices`.

Since Micronaut 4.10.18 the OpenAPI spec declares every `text/event-stream` response as an array of the event where it used to declare the event alone, and hey-api's SSE client then typed every streamed execution, log line or copilot chunk as `EventExecution[]` and the like, which broke the frontend type check. Add an `unwrapEventStreamArrayResponses` parser patch to the shared hey-api plugin that swaps such an array schema for its item schema, apply it in the OSS generator config and cover it with a unit test, so the generated event-stream types keep their previous shape.

Types and names, Imports, conventions the codebase already follows, and Tests.

SigV4Validator.java and RdsSigV4Validator.java both fell back to
`iamService.findSecretKey(accessKeyId).orElse(accessKeyId)` when the
access key wasn't registered. Since the attacker chooses accessKeyId
themselves, they can self-sign a token using secret == accessKeyId,
producing the exact signing key this fallback derives -- a full
signature-forgery auth bypass for any unregistered IAM key. Both now
fail closed when the key isn't registered.

also skipped the check whenever the token simply omitted the User
query param, letting any expectedUsername through. Dropped the
`user != null` conjunct so a null user now correctly fails the check.

fix(appconfig): accept top-level resource ARNs in TagResource/ListTagsForResource (#2279)
* fix(appconfig): accept top-level resource ARNs in TagResource/ListTagsForResource

AppConfigTagHandler#parseArn hardcoded the assumption that every AppConfig
resource ARN nests under application/... - true for environment and
configurationprofile, but AWS documents deploymentstrategy, extension, and
extensionassociation as top-level, taggable resources (see e.g. the Tags
property on AWS::AppConfig::DeploymentStrategy/Extension/ExtensionAssociation).
A deploymentstrategy/{id} ARN has parts[0] == "deploymentstrategy", not
"application", so it fell through to the 400 at the end of parseArn.

Adds a TOP_LEVEL_TYPES set for the three non-nested taggable types and checks
it before the application/ branch. Tag storage for these types remains a
no-op (same existing precedent as environment/configurationprofile) - this

fix(typescript-axios): resolve TS2527 inaccessible unique symbol error (#24526)
* fix(typescript-axios): resolve TS2527 inaccessible unique symbol error

createRequestFunction's returned arrow function lacked an explicit
return-type annotation. With axios >=1.19 (peer dep bumped to
^1.18.0 in b0670e28fcb), AxiosInstance.request<T, R>() defaults R to
a non-exported branded type backed by an unexported unique symbol,
and its return type is a conditional that only collapses once R is
concrete. Since our generic R stays unresolved through the call,
TypeScript must reference the inaccessible symbol when inferring the
exported function's type, causing TS2527.

Fix: annotate the arrow function with an explicit Promise<R> return
type and cast axios.request<T, R>(...)'s result with `as Promise<R>`
to satisfy the assignability check.

* fix(kotlin-spring, java-spring): gate @JsonSetter on openApiNullable for optional non-nullable fields

   For optional + non-nullable properties (required: false, nullable: false):
   - openApiNullable=false → @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.SKIP): silently ignores
     explicit JSON null, protecting any defined default from being overridden
   - openApiNullable=true → @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL): rejects explicit
     JSON null, enforcing the non-nullable contract (useful for PATCH semantics)

   Previously, Nulls.FAIL was unconditionally generated for all optional
   non-nullable fields regardless of openApiNullable, causing a breaking change
   for users on openApiNullable=false.

   Java Spring now also emits @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.SKIP) for the same case
   (previously it emitted nothing).

   Fixes #23976

[fix] Apply REMOVE_X_INTERNAL normalizer to nested inline properties (#22097)
* fix: Apply REMOVE_X_INTERNAL normalizer to nested inline properties

When REMOVE_X_INTERNAL=true is set, the normalizer removes the x-internal
extension from top-level schemas in components/schemas but fails to remove
it from inline object properties within those schemas.

This causes issues when:
1. A schema is imported cross-file (e.g., admin.yaml imports from chat.yaml)
2. That schema has an inline object property with x-internal: true
3. The inline property has type: object with nested properties

Result: TypeScript generator creates a type reference but no interface
definition, causing compilation errors.

This fix applies the same x-internal removal logic to normalizeProperties()
that already exists in normalizeComponentsSchemas(), ensuring inline
properties are handled consistently.

Fixes behavior for inline schemas with x-internal in cross-file imports.
